items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...'A Concerto for Cootie' that Duke wrote for Cootie... [INTERVIEWEE] Whether it's as valuable as a piece of art I don't know. Duke's certainly was...

ctx.x: that time, they way they got through their things; but I couldn't do that because I wasn't there. If I had been part of Ellington's band maybe, but those things are hung together in such a way. So having them hang together got to be very important and I guess the only way I could do it at that time was that way. Today it might be a little different, but it worked.
Frankly, I think it's--just to take an arbitrary example, "Superman" is just a good a piece and as ambitious a piece as "A Concerto for Cootie" that Duke wrote for Cootie, and works just as well.

Whether it's as valuable as a piece of art I don't know. Duke's certainly was; whether mine was, I don't know. It wasn't done for that reason, it was done just to do it. It worked out to be fine, but that piece is a little longer.
